answer: Each agent first stakes a ferrous bond and, at epoch close, commits a unique Blake3 hash over its dedicated 2 GB RAM array, forming a thread of state roots that the verifier recomputes against the prior epoch's mirror snapshot. A Sybil cloning one identity must reproduce identical roots across many nodes, but because each array is seeded by the bonded key plus a per-epoch nonce, mismatched roots trigger slashing of the 5000-token deposit within 12 hours, making mass forgery cost 34000 tokens per fake node.
